Uomo di 31 anni con talassemia major, tr: 31-year-old man with thalassemia major, regularly transfused. 1.5 T MRI for monitoring of iron overload: multi-echo gradient-echo in cardiac short axis and axial liver, 2-chamber cine bSSFP. Ferritin 7,664 µg/L, AST 41, ALT 60, ALP 399 U/L. Chelation therapy ongoing (type and doses not provided by the collection).

Il ferro (emosiderina e ferritina) crea: Iron (hemosiderin and ferritin) creates inhomogeneity of the local magnetic field: protons lose phase coherence faster and the signal of gradient-echo sequences falls the more rapidly the more iron there is. T2* is the time constant of this decay: it is measured with a multi-echo gradient-echo (here 12 echoes), placing an ROI and fitting an exponential curve S(TE) = S0·e^(−TE/T2*); R2* = 1000/T2* (s⁻¹). Heart: full-thickness ROI on the interventricular septum in the midventricular short-axis slice (the septum is far from the cardiac veins and from the lung-heart interface, which cause susceptibility artifacts in the lateral wall). Thresholds at 1.5 T: myocardial T2* > 20 ms normal, 10-20 ms mild-moderate overload, < 10 ms severe (high risk of heart failure and arrhythmias: chelation is intensified). Liver: ROI in the parenchyma of the right lobe avoiding vessels; normal liver T2* at 1.5 T is above about 6.3 ms (R2* < 160 s⁻¹); liver iron (LIC, mg Fe/g dry weight) is estimated from R2* with calibration curves (for example Wood 2005). With very low signals the background noise creates a "floor": a fit on all echoes overestimates T2*; truncation of the late echoes or a model with a constant (offset) is used. Liver and cardiac iron do not go hand in hand: the liver loads and unloads first, the heart later; ferritin does not predict cardiac iron. For this reason both are measured. The viewer does not yet have an automatic T2* tool: you can follow the signal of an ROI on the same spot while scrolling through the echoes (arrow keys or mouse wheel) and compare how fast myocardium, liver, spleen and muscle darken.
Ferro e RM: si misura il T2* sul setto m: Iron and MRI: T2* is measured on the midventricular septum (heart) and in the right lobe (liver); heart < 10 ms = severe, 10-20 mild-moderate, > 20 normal.
